messages:
From: Maya Torres <maya@aviationai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Weekend pilot: temporary throughput and SLA adjustment request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the call this week — our pilot for in-flight language moderation goes live for a controlled rollout this weekend and we expect a short, predictable spike in inference traffic. We’d like to request a temporary throughput/SLA uplift for the window so our engineers don’t get paged if throttling kicks in.

High-level ask: a temporary increase to burst capacity for route "flight-moderation" from 500 RPS to ~1,800 RPS for the window 2026-08-29 00:00 UTC to 2026-08-30 23:59 UTC. Latency SLO is 150ms p50 for the route; we understand that may not be guaranteed, but we need prioritized routing and reduced throttling while the pilot runs.

Attached is our expected traffic pattern (aviationai_weekend_traffic.csv) and a short sample of payloads. We can accept an abbreviated addendum (one-week temp exception) with clear rollback triggers.

Can you confirm what Redwood can provision and whether any credits/penalties apply if the increased throughput degrades other customers?

Best,
Maya Torres
Head of Platform
AviationAI

Attachment: aviationai_weekend_traffic.csv (CSV, 38KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Torres <maya@aviationai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Weekend pilot: temporary throughput/SLA adjustment request

Hi Maya — thanks for the details and the CSV. We can support a temporary exception for a short pilot window, but I want to align on the operational guardrails first. Quick clarifying questions:

- Is the 1,800 RPS estimate peak sustained or a short burst (seconds vs minutes)?
- Are you sending all traffic to a single model and route, or can you split lower-priority requests to a secondary route?
- Any data residency or VPC requirements for the weekend?

I've looped in Karthik (SRE/Capacity) and Marissa (CS lead) — please see the attached pilot_qa_checklist.pdf for our standard operational items.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to confirm whether we can apply a per-route temporary burst multiplier and the monitoring thresholds.
- We prepare a one-page addendum (temporary_sla_addendum.pdf) and DocuSign for signatures.
- Redwood will enable detailed token-level tracing for the route during the window.

I'll follow up with a concrete proposal by EOD.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot_qa_checklist.pdf (PDF, 24KB)

From: Maya Torres <maya@aviationai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 12:30:15 -0400
Subject: Re: Weekend pilot: temporary throughput/SLA adjustment request

Hi Tessa — thanks. Quick answers:
- 1,800 RPS is a short sustained peak for about 20–40 minutes each hour between 02:00 and 08:00 UTC (it’s correlated with transatlantic routes). Otherwise traffic falls to ~300–400 RPS.
- We send all moderation traffic to one logical route but can implement soft-fallbacks if you prefer (send low-priority video captions to a cheaper model).
- No special VPC or data residency needs for this pilot; standard hosted API is fine.

I've attached traffic_samples.jsonl with anonymized payloads. We are happy to sign an addendum for a two-day window.

Thanks,
Maya

Attachment: traffic_samples.jsonl (JSONL, 1.2MB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:05:30 -0400
Subject: Re: Weekend pilot: temporary throughput/SLA adjustment request

Tessa / Marissa — quick tech read on feasibility. Based on the traffic shape:

- We can apply a per-route temporary burst multiplier of 3x for the specified window for route "flight-moderation". That would take 500 RPS -> 1,500 RPS peak. Hitting 1,800 RPS briefly could be tolerated with autoscale and pre-warmed capacity, but it increases probability of cross-tenant tail latency.
- Mitigation: 1) enable spillover to a pre-warmed spare GPU pool for the weekend; 2) apply a soft-priority policy so non-essential tokens are rate-limited first; 3) enable aggressive KV-prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- SLAs: we cannot promise p50 150ms under sustained cross-tenant pressure; we can offer prioritized routing and best-effort p50 200ms with an operational playbook and monitoring. If we breach agreed availability thresholds due to our misrouting, we can discuss one-time credits (TBD).

Operational asks from AviationAI: commitment to the mutual action plan doc, access to a short alerting channel during the window, and permission to roll back the uplift if we detect material degradation for other customers.

If you want this approved, I'll need sign-off from capacity today so we can provision pre-warmed nodes.

—Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Torres <maya@aviationai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Weekend pilot: temporary throughput/SLA adjustment request

Thanks Karthik — that approach sounds reasonable. AviationAI agrees to:
- Sign the two-day addendum and accept rollback triggers for cross-tenant impact.
- Implement a soft-fallback for non-critical captions to the cheaper route.
- Provide an on-call Slack channel and a single technical contact (ops@aviationai.com).

Please send the DocuSign when ready and let us know the exact uplift numbers you will provision (1,500 RPS guaranteed burst, with best-effort handling above that).

Maya

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Torres <maya@aviationai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 17:10:45 -0400
Subject: Re: Weekend pilot: temporary throughput/SLA adjustment request

Hi all — confirming next steps and the temporary SLA carveout for AviationAI:

1) Uplift details: Redwood will apply a temporary per-route burst multiplier for route "flight-moderation" resulting in an assured burst capacity of 1,500 RPS for the window 2026-08-29 00:00 UTC through 2026-08-30 23:59 UTC. We will provision pre-warmed spare nodes to absorb short spikes; we will monitor and scale where possible.

2) Latency & availability: We will prioritize AviationAI traffic on best-effort p50 200ms target for the route during the window. This is an operational target, not a contractual long-term SLA. If Redwood’s routing or capacity management causes an availability incident beyond 5% degraded requests over a one-hour window, we will discuss a one-time credit (amount to be agreed in the addendum).

3) Rollback & safeguards: Redwood reserves the right to rollback the uplift immediately if we detect material cross-tenant degradation. We will notify AviationAI via the on-call Slack and email and provide a post-mortem within 48 hours if rollback occurs.

4) Paperwork: Attached is the temporary_sla_addendum.pdf and a DocuSign link (https://www.docusign.com/temporary-addendum/4421). Please sign before 2026-08-29 00:00 UTC.

5) Monitoring: We will enable token-level tracing and share a short dashboard with AviationAI. Karthik will be on-call for the weekend.

I'll kick off provisioning now and send a confirmation when the route is pre-warmed. Thanks for being flexible — this should enable a smooth pilot without requiring long-term commitment.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: temporary_sla_addendum.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
